screening.reason: Inclusion 2-3: ABIDE I+II rs-fMRI functional connectivity used to classify ASD vs TD and to study how population diversity affects predictive accuracy and pattern stability.

evidence_spans.text:
procedures resulted in a total of 297 par-
ticipants (151 ASD and 146 TD) from 4 different sites (i.e., New York University Langone
Medical Center [NYU], University of Pittsburgh, School of Medicine [PITT], University of
Utah, School of Medicine [USM], and Trinity Centre for Health Sciences [TCD]) in ABIDE.
evidence_spans.claim: Final ABIDE sample: 297 participants (151 ASD, 146 TD) from 4 sites (NYU, PITT, USM, TCD).

evidence_spans.text:
For ABIDE, we considered data from all acquisition sites with at least 10 participants per
group and with both children and adults. After detailed quality control, only cases with accept-
able T1-weighted (T1w) MRI, surface extraction, and head motion in rs-fMRI were included.
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE sites required at least 10 participants per group and both children and adults; QC required acceptable T1w MRI, surface extraction, and acceptable head motion in rs-fMRI.

evidence_spans.text:
Participants with ASD were diagnosed based on an in-person interview administered by
board-certified mental health professionals using the gold standard diagnostics of the Autism
Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) [51] and/or Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised
(ADI-R) [52,53].
evidence_spans.claim: ASD diagnosis was based on an in-person interview using ADOS and/or ADI-R gold-standard diagnostics.

evidence_spans.text:
For the resting-state functional brain scans in ABIDE, we built on data previously made
available by the Preprocessed Connectomes initiative (http://preprocessed-connectomes-
project.org/abide). The preprocessing was performed with C-PAC (https://fcp-indi.github.io)
and included slice time correction, head motion correction, skull stripping, and intensity nor-
malization. The rs-fMRI data were detrended and adjusted for common nuisance effects
related to head motion, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid signals using CompCor [58], fol-
lowed by band-pass filtering (0.01 to 0.1 Hz).
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE rs-fMRI was preprocessed via the Preprocessed Connectomes initiative using C-PAC (slice-time correction, motion correction, skull stripping, intensity normalization, CompCor, band-pass filtering).

evidence_spans.text:
Func-
tional connectivity matrices were calculated at a single-participant level based on a widely used
parcellation atlas with 100 cortical regions [61].
evidence_spans.claim: Functional connectivity matrices were computed using a 100-region (Schaefer-Yeo) cortical parcellation atlas.

evidence_spans.text:
After matching, we ended up with 290 participants (145 participants per group)
in ABIDE and 126 (63 participants per group) in HBN, which were used subsequently for the
classification of ASD versus TD in both datasets.
evidence_spans.claim: After propensity-score matching on age, sex and site, 290 ABIDE participants (145 per group) were used for classification.

evidence_spans.text:
Similar to the computation of the pro-
pensity scores, we performed deconfounding prior to our analyses, based on all the available
participants instead of using only the training
evidence_spans.claim: Propensity scores and deconfounding were computed using all available participants rather than training data only.

evidence_spans.text:
In the ABIDE cohort, when we trained and
tested on data with similar distributions (first column), the contiguous scheme reached better
prediction performance than the diverse scheme, with the random scheme lying in between.
This trend remained stable as we increased the number of strata used for training.
evidence_spans.claim: In ABIDE, training and testing on similarly-distributed (contiguous) strata achieved better prediction than diverse strata.

evidence_spans.text:
we can observe a decline in performance in ABIDE as diversity increased in both within
(AUC: r = −0.630, F1 score: r = −0.568) and out-of-distribution (AUC: r = −0.671, F1 score:
r = −0.579) predictions.
evidence_spans.claim: In ABIDE, prediction performance declined as participant diversity increased, both within-distribution (AUC r=-0.630) and out-of-distribution (AUC r=-0.671).

evidence_spans.text:
Data Availability Statement: The imaging and
phenotypic data were provided, in part, by the
Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange initiative
(ABIDE-I and II; https://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.
org/indi/abide) and the Healthy Brain Network
(https://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/cmi_
healthy_brain_network). All imaging features,
phenotypic data, and code are openly available at
https://github.com/OualidBenkarim/ps_diversity.
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE/HBN imaging and phenotypic data, all imaging features, phenotypic data, and analysis code are openly available on GitHub.

assessments.support: Explicit per-site inclusion threshold (>=10/group), QC criteria, diagnosis via ADOS/ADI-R, and final N by diagnosis and site are all reported.
C-PAC preprocessing pipeline and a named 100-region (Schaefer-Yeo) atlas are explicitly reported.
Binary ASD vs TD classification with diagnosis sourced from gold-standard ADOS/ADI-R instruments.

The paper explicitly states that propensity-score computation and deconfounding (linear regression and ComBat) were performed using all available participants rather than confined to the training data, a form of information leakage the authors themselves flag and partially probe (Fig 4).

risk_of_bias.summary: Methodologically rich and transparent (open code/data, explicit QC, named pipeline/atlas), but the authors' own text documents that propensity-score and deconfounding computations used the full sample rather than training folds only, a PROBAST-relevant leakage concern in the Analysis domain.

charting.title: Population heterogeneity in clinical cohorts affects the predictive accuracy of brain imaging
charting.authors: Oualid Benkarim; Casey Paquola; Bo-yong Park; et al.
charting.primary_focus: Effect of population heterogeneity/diversity on predictive accuracy and pattern stability
charting.primary_goal: Quantify how demographic/site diversity (via propensity scores) affects cross-validated prediction accuracy and biomarker pattern stability in ASD classification
charting.country_region: Multi-site (4 ABIDE sites: NYU, PITT, USM, TCD)
charting.diagnosis_assessment: ADOS and/or ADI-R gold-standard diagnostics via in-person interview by board-certified mental health professionals
charting.n_disordered: 151 (297 total before matching); 145 after propensity-score matching
charting.comorbidities_included_excluded: Excluded: genetic disorders associated with autism (e.g. Fragile X), MRI contraindications, current pregnancy
charting.n_controls: 146 (297 total before matching); 145 after propensity-score matching
charting.age_matched: true (propensity-score matched on age, sex, site)
charting.dataset_openly_available: Yes — all imaging features, phenotypic data and analysis code openly available at https://github.com/OualidBenkarim/ps_diversity; figure data in S1 Data
charting.specific_features: Region-to-region functional connectivity using a 100-region Schaefer-Yeo cortical parcellation atlas
charting.feature_extraction_tools: C-PAC (Preprocessed Connectomes Project pipeline: slice-time correction, motion correction, skull stripping, intensity normalization, CompCor, band-pass filtering 0.01-0.1 Hz); FreeSurfer for structural/cortical thickness
charting.importance_method: Model coefficient (weight vector) consistency via Pearson correlation across resampled models
charting.model_category: Linear classifier (predictive modeling of ASD vs TD from functional connectivity)
charting.validation_methodology: Propensity-score-based stratified train/holdout partitioning (contiguous, diverse, random sampling schemes) with 10-fold CV within training strata; out-of-distribution evaluation on held-out strata
charting.key_performance_results: ABIDE: prediction performance declined as diversity increased — within-distribution AUC r=-0.630, F1 r=-0.568; out-of-distribution AUC r=-0.671, F1 r=-0.579. Deconfounding (linear regression r=-0.539; ComBat r=-0.599) only slightly reduced this correlation versus raw data (r=-0.671).
charting.summary_key_findings: In ABIDE (and oppositely in HBN), predictive accuracy and pattern stability for ASD vs TD classification decline substantially as population diversity (quantified via propensity scores on age, sex, site) increases, and this effect persists after standard deconfounding (linear regression or ComBat), which were themselves computed using all participants rather than training data only.
charting.reviewer_notes: Important methodological finding: propensity-score and deconfounding computations used the full dataset (not train-only), a leakage concern the authors themselves report.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction study; ABIDE I+II, final N=297 (151 ASD, 146 TD) from 4 sites (NYU, PITT, USM, TCD), reduced to N=290 (145/145) after propensity-score matching on age, sex and site.
narrative_row.methods: Rs-fMRI preprocessed with C-PAC (Preprocessed Connectomes Project); functional connectivity via a 100-region Schaefer-Yeo atlas; ASD vs TD classification under contiguous/diverse/random training-stratum sampling schemes with 10-fold CV, evaluated within- and out-of-distribution; linear-regression and ComBat deconfounding tested.
narrative_row.outcomes: Prediction accuracy (AUC, F1) and extracted-pattern stability declined as participant diversity increased in ABIDE (opposite direction to HBN); deconfounding only partially reduced this diversity-performance relationship.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Propensity-score and deconfounding computations used the full sample rather than training-fold-only data, a leakage concern flagged by the authors; negligible female representation in ABIDE (<0.02%) limited sex-related analysis.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Directly interrogates how ABIDE's site/demographic composition (diversity) affects reproducibility of predictive findings; open code and data make the analysed cohort reconstructible; illustrates a leakage pattern (full-sample deconfounding) relevant to RQ4/CL5 across the corpus.

kg_link.cohort_description: 297 participants (151 ASD, 146 TD) from 4 ABIDE sites (NYU, PITT, USM, TCD) meeting per-site N>=10/group and QC criteria; reduced to 290 (145/145) after propensity-score matching on age, sex, site.
kg_link.finding: ASD vs TD classification accuracy and extracted-pattern stability decline as participant diversity (propensity-score based) increases in ABIDE (within-distribution AUC r=-0.630; out-of-distribution AUC r=-0.671), the opposite relationship found in the HBN cohort.
